answer: Rotating beacon attestation slots.** Each period, a shared public beacon assigns each identity one narrow, unpredictable slot to countersign a prior agent's transaction batch; miss it and your identity is suspended for the next period. Cloning forces the attacker to hold and actively answer every clone's assigned slot — a per-identity availability cost paid continuously. A client can require co-signed history on an onyx ledger before trusting an identity. Critically, the beacon's schedule is derived from a ridge of past entropy the attacker cannot precompute,
